relevance_note: Case series of three unrelated patients with heterozygous TNFAIP3 variants and lupus nephritis, with individual-level detail: 'Here we describe three unrelated patients with autoimmune lupus nephritis (LN) phenotypes carrying three novel mutations in the TNFAIP3 gene.'
method_note: Read the full paper; rows were written by a Python script whose content was typed from my reading; table-row spans were cut from the paper lines by the script and every span checked verbatim. Tables 1-3 have patients as columns (headers 'Patient 1', 'Patient 2', 'Patient 3'); the text label 'P1'/'P2'/'P3' is used because the text uses it most. Scope: P1-P3 plus relatives described in relation to them: P1's mother (recurrent oral ulcers; Table 1 'Mutation origin: From mother'), P1's son (6 years, features listed; the paper says only that the mutation 'co-segregated with disease phenotype in the family', so no variant row for the son), P2's two parents (tested negative; sex not stated), P3's asymptomatic mother (carrier). P3's father and 'other family members' tested by Sanger are not described individually and get no rows. Six adult and three child healthy controls get no rows. Table 1 cells reading 'No' were taken as explicit absence of that category (Recurrent fever, Serositis, Musculoskeletal, Ocular, Cardiovascular); a broad 'Musculoskeletal: No' / 'Ocular: No' was used to exclude the narrower checklist items arthritis or arthralgia / ocular inflammation. Table 2 'Absent'/'Present' words used as stated. Table 3 empty cell (P1 dsDNA) and ND cells (P1 CRP/ESR, P3 IgE) treated as not reported. Group statements used: 'proteinuria and haematuria without renal insufficiency' (the three patients), 'Elevated serum cytokine IL-6 levels in the three patients', 'All were strongly positive for ANA and/or anti-dsDNA and had decreased C3 and C4 levels', and 'novel pathogenic mutations' for the three patients' variants (not applied to the carrier mothers). Age at diagnosis records the genetic-diagnosis age; Table 1 also gives age at LN diagnosis (29, 3, 3). Ages in the text ('29-year-old', '3-year-old girl') coincide with LN diagnosis, so age at last evaluation is left not reported; follow-up durations 6.5, 2 and 1.5 years are in Table 4. P2 had no autoantibodies during the first year and later developed them; this is a change over time, not a contradiction, so only the later positive status is recorded. Table 3 'Other autoantibodies: Negative' for P2 recorded as excluded other autoantibodies alongside positive ANA/dsDNA. P3's mother is described only as 'asymptomatic'; no feature rows were made from this global statement. Thrombocytopenia in P1 is not called autoimmune, so checklist 'cytopenia (autoimmune)' left not reported for P1; P1's son's 'anaemia' likewise. Son's Henoch-Schonlein purpura diagnosis recorded as a feature but not mapped to the vasculitis checklist item. Table 5 common SLE risk alleles (other genes) were not recorded as variant rows (risk alleles, excluded by scope). No contradictions inside the paper found.
